claims.text: Lower-temperature ZrB2 produced around 1700 °C is easier to manufacture than ZrB2 produced above 2300 °C.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 has inadequate oxidation resistance.
Lower-temperature ZrB2 is susceptible to corrosion by liquid plating metals.
Single-phase ZrB2 produced above 2300 °C has ideal mechanical and high-temperature properties.
Producing single-phase ZrB2 above 2300 °C is energy intensive.
CoCrFeNiMo0.85 can be made into an electrode and deposited as a high-entropy-alloy coating by electro spark deposition.
A CoCrFeNiMo0.85 coating can be deposited successfully onto a ZrB2 substrate by electro spark deposition.
The coating operation can be performed at a processing temperature below 1700 °C.
Electro spark deposition of CoCrFeNiMo0.85 on ZrB2 will form a compact, homogeneous, adherent coating.
The deposited coating will form a graded interface with ZrB2.
The compact coating will prevent or reduce oxygen ingress into ZrB2.
The coating will prevent direct contact between ZrB2 and liquid plating metal.
The CoCrFeNiMo-based coating has sufficient inherent high-temperature chemical stability to resist oxidation during the proposed service.
Inhibiting direct interaction between liquid metal and ZrB2 will mitigate liquid-metal corrosion.
The coated lower-temperature ZrB2 will have mechanical strength similar to high-temperature single-phase ZrB2.
The coating will maintain the strength and structural integrity of lower-temperature ZrB2.
Coated ZrB2 will resist oxidation significantly better than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and uncoated lower-temperature ZrB2.
Coated ZrB2 will resist liquid-metal corrosion significantly better than both high-temperature single-phase ZrB2 and uncoated lower-temperature ZrB2.
The protective benefits will persist during prolonged liquid-plating-metal exposure while the HEA coating remains thermally intact.

contradictions.description: The design specifies only coated and uncoated lower-temperature groups, but the falsification rule also requires comparison with a high-temperature ZrB2 baseline that is not included as an experimental group.
